records.title: High-dose spinal cord stimulation for patients with failed back surgery syndrome: a multicenter effectiveness and prediction study

searches.service: Internet Archive capture of LWW publisher full text
searches.query: 10.1097/j.pain.0000000000002035 exact holistic-responder thresholds and model split

updates.ограничения: Publisher full text defines a 12-month holistic responder requiring all four changes: 33% improvement in both low-back and leg NRS, 30% ODI improvement, EQ-5D increase of at least 0.03, and medication decrease. A distinct four-week trial-success rule uses 50% pain and medication reduction and must not be substituted. The primary article reports 80/20 train-validation and five random validation sets, but no prediction-specific N, per-split denominators, split unit or patient-disjointness. No external validation or ECAP; related Discover-registry cohorts may overlap. Live LWW access is restricted; review used a 2021 capture of the publisher page.

validation.notes.value: The 2021 Internet Archive capture of the original LWW publisher full text was reviewed directly on 2026-09-27; live LWW access returned 403. Methods §2.5 and Figure 3 define the four-part 12-month holistic response; separate four-week trial-success thresholds are not interchangeable. Logistic/CART methods report 80/20 train-validation with five random validation sets. Cohort flow is 194 recruited, 185 baseline and 92 remaining on HD-SCS at 12 months, but prediction-specific N, absolute split Ns, patient-disjointness and row linkage are not printed. No ECAP predictor or external cohort is established.
